As a foreigner, I was greatly impressed by this public hospital. Yes, the building is old and some of the workers there can be a little rude, but they work hard all day, so it’s understandable that they might be tired.
I went there because I was feeling pressure in my chest, and my doctor advised me to go to the hospital. They did a blood pressure test, a chest X-ray, and a heart test. After that, a doctor examined me and gave her diagnosis and medication.
For all that, I paid 750 baht and stayed for around 1 hour and 30 minutes. Great service and an unbelievable price compared to a private hospital, where I would have paid around 30–40k for the same thing.

Visited Krabi Provincial Hospital when my wife was severely dehydrated, pale, and unable to keep fluids down. Using Google Translate, we communicated her condition clearly. Within 5 minutes, she was on a gurney in the ER, and within an hour, she had an IV. The staff handled everything efficiently despite the busy environment. We were in and out in 3 hours, and the total cost, including IV and meds, was only 1,500 THB (~$45). Impressive care for us farangs from California—highly recommend!

This place seems terribly understaffed and they're all overworked and/or just don't care about patients.  Or maybe its something against farang patients, I don't know, but many of the staff (not All... 1 or 2 were very nice and helpful) ...were quite rude.  My husband was in for a surgery for 3 days and they act annoyed any time he asked for ANYthing... he couldn't walk after surgery on his leg and they would not even help him to the toilet, or give him any pain meds for the last 24hours he was there.

underrated hospital. Typical Thai quality of medical services. Long beaurocracy, poor English among supporting personel (registry, nurses), high expertise and level of English among doctors. I came with a barotrauma after scuba diving. Got adequate examination and treatment. Just get ready it will take you hours to see the doctor.
Minus 1 star for the desire to charnge more. :D There was no way they were going to let a farang leave having paid 300 baht for a proper doctor visit and medicine (160b for doctor and 145 for 4 medications prescribed). So, they insisted on varios uneeded examinations (like, fiber optics ear chanel scan, which I said I do not need, I trust the doctor's examination. She did the same examination with a simple tube and her eyes are much more trained to see if something's wrong than mine). Fiber optics scan cost 2250 baht lol. But come on. Bare with it. Be greatful to Thais who take care of you

I had to get treatment & injections after getting attacked by a wild dog. It left me with open wounds in my leg, also I needed rabies treatment. Upon arrival the staff placed me on a stretcher with a plastic surface that already had big brown and red blood stains on it - and those definitely weren't mine! I'm so glad I was conscious enough to keep the injured parts of my leg up in the air. I had to keep my leg propped up the whole time I was in the ER, all through examinations, wound treatment and rabies shots into the wounds. Nobody offered a clean examination table, although I specifically asked for it.
Staff spoke almost no English, but that's fair enough. Treatment of wounds went ok, however they didn't use any anaesthesia on wounds that definitely would have needed some. This seemed to be a pattern, I saw other patients in the ER who could have used painkillers but weren't given any during their treatments either - even kids!
All in all they do their job in keeping you alive, but be aware of really poor hygiene and rough handling in the ER.

I have been very impressed and satisfied by the dedication and knowledge of the people running this hospital. Of course, you will have to queue up for any demand as it is a very very busy place and every patient is treated without any financial preferences. Bravo Thailand !

It was an unexpectedly impressive experience. All the nurses and staff were very polite and spoke kindly. While some might need to adjust their language, I was particularly impressed with Ms. Siriporn Boonthavorn, the gynecology nurse at …

The staff and nurses provide excellent service. The waiting area is at examination room 9 in the 65-year-old building. The air-conditioned ward on the ground floor is cool and comfortable. The nurses are diligent, especially in the mornings, helping patients' relatives change linens and bathe them. They work until late in the day; I feel tired just watching them.
The private rooms on the 6th and 7th floors also have diligent nurses who provide good care and offer various recommendations. Plus, the view is probably one of the most beautiful in Krabi, better than most hotel views. The rooms are clean, and the housekeeping staff are hardworking.

Another place that impressed me is the X-ray room (located in front of the shrine). The staff are lovely and very polite.

The service was terrible, absolutely awful, especially the staff member calling out patient names outside room 11 on March 10th, 1969 at 11:30 AM. They had a displeased expression. We heard them call our name, but when we arrived, they said …

text:
As a French couple visiting Krabi for a holiday, we needed to see a doctor for a respiratory infection.

We were taken care of immediately upon arrival at this Krabi hospital, and despite the significant language barrier, the staff did everything they could to help us, tested us for COVID-19, and directed us to the emergency room to be seen by a doctor. The wait was very short, and the doctor's explanations were clear thanks to our willingness to use Google Translate.
We were directed to the nurses, received our medication at the hospital very quickly, and settled the bill for our treatment (2420 baht / 66 euros for both of us).
The staff were helpful, friendly, and attentive to our needs via Google Translate. They didn't hesitate to advise us to return to the hospital if any complications arose within two days.
We highly recommend this hospital.

Terrible. Brought my father to the emergency room with diarrhea and vomiting. He submitted the card room card and had a queue card for medicine, but there was no notification of where to put the queue card. After that, a nurse called out in …

Today I had the opportunity to receive medical services and was treated exceptionally well by the nurses, staff, and assistants. Everyone was wonderful, attentive, and provided excellent care and advice. Above all, I would like to express my sincere commendation to Dr. Bulawat Kuncharin, the internal medicine doctor. He is one of the best doctors I have ever received treatment from. He inquired about my symptoms, was attentive, asked about the cause, treatment options, and analyzed the various symptoms very well. He was calm, spoke kindly, and was easy to understand. A good doctor should be like this. Dr. Kitipat also gave excellent advice. I wish that medical personnel and new doctors who come to treat people were as good as these two doctors. The people of Krabi would then be reassured that they have good doctors taking care of them.
Finally, I would like to offer my encouragement to all medical personnel and thank you for taking care of the public who use your services.

My sister was admitted to Krabi Hospital with a bronchial infection and a very high fever of 39 degrees Celsius. We waited for about two hours. When it was our turn, she was called to the examination room. The doctor asked what was wrong, …

The male patient was in the ward all day without being called. When it was time to go home, they told the relatives to wait to talk to the doctor first. We waited for hours and they still didn't come. It was a huge waste of time!

I have to come here regularly because it's the hospital near my home. They're improving, although I've encountered some staff members who are a bit rude to patients, but I understand that there are a lot of patients every day, so I have to accept that. It would be much better if they built a proper parking lot or parking building with enough parking spaces to accommodate everyone daily, so that cars coming to the hospital don't park haphazardly outside, blocking public transport stops, or causing problems for surrounding businesses by parking for extended periods.

Urgently improve the staff here. It's a waste of money hiring them. Examinations were completed by 10 am, but by 2 or 3 pm the doctor still hadn't arrived. They spoke rudely and treated patients like beggars. They said there was only one …

After a scooter accident, I was taken by ambulance to Hospital Krabi.
The doctors and nurses responded and treated me as best they could, taking into account the other patients. They did an X-ray, ultrasound and MRI. I was hospitalized for 4 days with suspicion of internal bleeding. The nurses and doctors took excellent care of me, I was bedridden. My boyfriend took care of me at the bedside the whole time and there was no problem with that. We had all the conversations through a translator, because we don't speak English or Thai. The only thing that was tiring for me was the heat and only fans, a large room with about 30 beds and a lot of relatives of the patients who are here 24/7.
The staff was incredibly nice, smiling, dedicated.
The longest part was waiting to complete the formalities with the insurance companies for payment of the hospitalization.

My son had a motorcycle accident during his vacation in Krabi, and unfortunately, it was the most horrible experience of my life in that hospital! The intensive care unit was in a deplorable state! He's been traumatized ever since!

Emergency service is very bad. I'm a tourist and have to wait a long time. They bring a chair to sit and check on the patient's condition. The nurse told me to bring the chair back to its original place. The chair that was brought up was …

text:
My car was blocking the road. I called the information desk, but they said the loudspeaker system was broken and couldn't help. I had another appointment and couldn't keep it. It was inconvenient and the service was terrible.

The information desk then suggested I contact the security guard, but he refused to answer. They might as well not hire security guards; it's a waste of hospital funds.

Interpersonal relationships are terrible, there's a lot of discrimination, and if you're a foreigner, you'll be called last. He's very talkative and hard to find in the doctor's office; they're on the phone all the time. I see the younger teachers often.

The parking lot should be renovated and improved. The parking lot is terrible. It is full of potholes, making it very difficult for low-level vehicles to enter and pass through. It is constantly scraped. Especially during the rainy season, it is very bad. If you are not going to renovate it, you should do something about the deep potholes. It would be good to use rocks and sand to fill them in.

The care for patients in the private rooms is quite good.
The downside is that while waiting in line at the outpatient building, on the side near the casting rooms (8-11), there's a very strong cigarette smell. People are smoking heavily in front of the men's restroom next to the building, even though there's a sign saying "No Smoking!" The smell is constantly blowing into the waiting area throughout the 2-3 hours I've been waiting.
I would appreciate it if the staff could warn them or check on the situation occasionally.

The service was excellent. This was my first time using their services. The nurses, doctors, and hospital staff were all incredibly kind, polite, and always smiling, even though there were so many patients. The doctor conducted a very thorough examination. I was very impressed and felt very reassured. Thank you so much!
Terrible! My finger came off and I've been sitting here for two hours straight. They haven't even called me.

Terrible service, especially in the emergency room. My partner had a severe allergic reaction, but we were made to wait for a doctor. His face and body were swollen, and he had difficulty breathing, but we were still told to "wait for the doctor." The nurses were also rude and impolite. I once took my niece there because someone accidentally mixed the wrong formula with water used for mopping the floor, and the nurse said we had to wait for the child to have a seizure before calling emergency services? I want them to improve. Young children cannot wait. My niece was drooling, but we were made to wait 3 hours. Where is the emergency room? They should change the name of the room. The nurses need to improve their behavior and receive some training. We're paying for medical treatment, we're not getting it for free. 🥱

text: Terrible! I came to the emergency room, but I still have to wait a long time. An emergency should be faster than this. People who are in critical condition shouldn't have to wait any longer. Improve this immediately!

The rating is based on the good medical team, but it doesn't overshadow the negative experience with the nurses. My father was admitted as an inpatient, and the illness itself was already upsetting enough, but the service from some of the nurses was even worse—I'd even describe it as terrible. I understand it's a public hospital, but if I had a choice, I wouldn't want to come here at all. This incident (though it might just be my experience) is particularly problematic. Today, I went to call a nurse because my father complained of severe phlegm and difficulty breathing. I informed the nurse, but they didn't provide immediate assistance. When I returned to the patient's bed, he said he couldn't breathe anymore, so I had to go back again. The response I received was one of dissatisfaction and a tone of voice. If they don't want to work, why are they there? Patients and their families are already uncomfortable at the hospital, and then they have to deal with such hurtful words and actions from government staff. When I followed up repeatedly, they scolded the family for disturbing the patient and preventing him from resting. Seriously, what were they thinking? Who wants to disturb a patient? Everyone wants the patient to rest. But since he reported pain and difficulty breathing, what were we supposed to do? Shouldn't we believe the nurse or the patient himself? And what I want to focus on the most is that you spoke to the patient and took your emotions out on them by suctioning phlegm so forcefully. Is that acceptable? It's terrible. If I had a choice, I wouldn't want to come here again, and if possible, I would report this to everyone I know and would not recommend this place to anyone. It's awful.
